label: Destructive inundation
inclusion_rule: Water inundation is itself a major destructive event affecting settlements/people/land.
exclusion_rule: Do not require near-total human destruction; do not code routine seasonal flooding.

label: Exterminatory deluge
inclusion_rule: The inundation is intended or described as destroying most/all humanity or the inhabited world.
exclusion_rule: Do not code flood-control or local destructive flooding without broad human-destruction claim.

label: Advance supernatural warning
inclusion_rule: A supernatural/divine/extraordinary agent gives advance information enabling preparation for the flood.
exclusion_rule: Ordinary observation or post-event revelation does not count.

label: Selected survivor group
inclusion_rule: One person/family/small selected group is specifically preserved while a much larger population is destroyed/threatened.
exclusion_rule: A flood-control official or generic survivors without selection do not count.

label: Floating vessel refuge
inclusion_rule: Survival depends on a deliberately used boat/ark/chest/raft or comparable floating container.
exclusion_rule: Travel by ordinary boat unrelated to flood survival does not count.

label: Elevated refuge
inclusion_rule: Survival depends on mountain/tree/tower/other elevated refuge above floodwaters.
exclusion_rule: A vessel merely landing on a mountain afterward does not count.

label: Post-flood ritual or sacrifice
inclusion_rule: Survivor performs sacrifice/offering/ritual soon after survival or recession of waters.
exclusion_rule: Later unrelated cult practice does not count.

label: Post-flood human renewal
inclusion_rule: Narrative explicitly addresses restoration/repopulation/recreation of humanity after flood.
exclusion_rule: Survival alone does not count.

label: Scout tests recession/land
inclusion_rule: After the flood/inundation peak, a person or nonhuman agent is deliberately sent/released to test whether land, habitability, or receded water can be established.
exclusion_rule: Animals appearing incidentally, omen-reading unrelated to recession, or ordinary reconnaissance outside flood survival do not count.

label: Human formed from earth/dust
inclusion_rule: Human body is made from generic loose earth, soil, dust or ground material, with no explicit plastic/wet quality.
exclusion_rule: Explicit clay, mud, wet/plastic earth, or an explicitly plastic operation such as kneading is coded under ANTH_CLAY_MUD instead; sibling motifs are mutually exclusive.

label: Human formed from clay/mud
inclusion_rule: Human body is made from clay, mud, wet/plastic earth, or earth explicitly manipulated as plastic material (for example kneaded).
exclusion_rule: Generic loose earth/dust without wet/plastic quality does not count; sibling ANTH_EARTH_DUST is mutually exclusive.

label: Potter-like forming
inclusion_rule: Human creation explicitly uses a craft-forming operation such as kneading, molding, shaping by hand, or a potter wheel.
exclusion_rule: A generic verb meaning create/form alone, or the mere presence/mixing of clay, is insufficient without an explicit craft-forming operation.

label: Divine/supernatural body material
inclusion_rule: The material of human formation explicitly incorporates blood, flesh, body matter or remains of a deity/supernatural being.
exclusion_rule: If human groups or social categories arise from division of a primordial being, code ANTH_BODY_SACRIFICE instead; the sibling motifs do not co-fire on one passage.

label: Breath/wind animates human
inclusion_rule: Breath, wind, spirit-breath or an equivalent animating principle is explicitly infused into an already formed human body.
exclusion_rule: Speech-only creation and a divine spirit/body component merely mixed into creation material are insufficient.

label: Humans created for divine service/labour
inclusion_rule: Text explicitly states humans are created to perform labour, cult, maintenance, or service for gods.
exclusion_rule: Later social duty or worship not given as creation purpose does not count.

label: Humans/social order from primordial body sacrifice
inclusion_rule: Human groups or human social categories arise explicitly from the division/sacrifice of a primordial being.
exclusion_rule: Divine body material merely incorporated into human formation is ANTH_DIVINE_BLOOD_FLESH, not this motif; the sibling motifs do not co-fire.

label: Explicit first human pair
inclusion_rule: Humanity descends from or begins with an explicitly first male-female/couple pair.
exclusion_rule: A survivor couple after a flood is separate unless narrative makes them first humans.

label: Humans formed from plant/wood material
inclusion_rule: Human bodies are explicitly made from wood, reeds, plants, gourds, maize/plant matter, or another plant-derived substance.
exclusion_rule: Plant food consumed by already created humans, metaphorical plant ancestry, or wooden images not becoming humans do not count.

label: Failed human creation precedes successful humans
inclusion_rule: The narrative explicitly describes one or more attempted human creations that fail, are destroyed, or are rejected before a successful human form/population.
exclusion_rule: Different human groups created for different purposes, or a flood destroying existing humans without a creation-attempt frame, do not count.

label: Speech/naming directly creates humans
inclusion_rule: Spoken command, naming, or performative speech directly brings a human being/population into existence or life.
exclusion_rule: Breath/wind infusion is ANTH_BREATH_ANIMATION; speech that merely instructs another creator does not count.

label: Multiple ontologically distinct creation materials
inclusion_rule: Derived flag: two or more independently coded material motifs co-occur in the same creation event.
exclusion_rule: Never hand-code as an independent motif and never include alongside its component motifs in primary similarity.

label: Primordial waters
inclusion_rule: Cosmic/terrestrial order begins with, emerges from, or is initially dominated by primordial waters.
exclusion_rule: Ordinary seas created after cosmic order or later floodwaters do not count.

label: Heaven-earth separation
inclusion_rule: Creation/cosmic ordering explicitly requires separating previously joined or contiguous sky/heaven and earth.
exclusion_rule: Merely listing heaven and earth as distinct realms does not count.

label: Cosmic egg/container
inclusion_rule: The cosmos or major primordial beings emerge from an egg-like enclosed primordial container explicitly functioning as a generative vessel.
exclusion_rule: Any ordinary egg birth or metaphorical roundness alone does not count.

label: Primordial body becomes world
inclusion_rule: Body parts/material of a primordial being become structural components of the world/cosmos.
exclusion_rule: Human/social groups from a body are anthropogony; defeated-enemy body in a conflict may also satisfy the narrower DIV_BODY_TO_COSMOS and must be tagged as a cross-family linked event.

label: Cosmic axis connects levels
inclusion_rule: A tree, mountain, pillar, rope, ladder, or equivalent structure explicitly connects two or more cosmic levels.
exclusion_rule: A sacred mountain/tree without a connecting function does not count.

label: Order from undifferentiated state
inclusion_rule: The narrative explicitly contrasts an earlier unseparated/formless/undifferentiated state with a later differentiated cosmic order.
exclusion_rule: Researcher-imposed labels such as 'chaos' without textual structural contrast do not count.

label: Speech/decree creates cosmic entities
inclusion_rule: Speech, naming, or decree directly brings cosmic entities/structures into existence.
exclusion_rule: Speech merely announces or commands a separate physical creation process does not count.

label: Explicit layered cosmos
inclusion_rule: The narrative explicitly distinguishes at least three ordered cosmic realms/levels such as sky, earth, underworld.
exclusion_rule: A binary heaven-earth contrast alone does not count.

label: Younger divine generation displaces older
inclusion_rule: A younger divine generation or younger deity actually defeats, displaces, or is acclaimed/decreed as having displaced an older ruling divine generation.
exclusion_rule: A merely foretold, feared or potential future displacement does not count; direction is fixed to younger displacing older.

label: Father-son succession conflict
inclusion_rule: Divine kingship/supremacy conflict is explicitly structured between a father and his son as the principal opposing parties.
exclusion_rule: A paternal plot frame or other kinship relation does not count unless the actual opposing parties are father and son.

label: Storm deity versus serpent/dragon
inclusion_rule: A storm/thunder-associated deity battles a serpent/dragon/serpentine adversary.
exclusion_rule: Sea deity without serpent/dragon identity is separate.

label: Storm deity versus sea/water deity
inclusion_rule: A storm/thunder-associated deity battles a personified sea/water deity or sovereign aquatic opponent.
exclusion_rule: Serpent/dragon opponent is separate unless text explicitly identifies both.

label: Defeated being becomes cosmos
inclusion_rule: Material from a defeated primordial/divine opponent becomes components of world/cosmos.
exclusion_rule: Death of enemy alone does not count.

label: Divine council deliberation
inclusion_rule: A plurality of gods explicitly acts as a collective deliberative/judicial body to decide, judge, assign roles or allocate authority.
exclusion_rule: A mere list/group of gods or private counsel among a small set of related deities does not count.

label: Transfer of divine kingship
inclusion_rule: Legitimate divine kingship/sovereignty is narrated or acclaimed as actually transferred between deities or generations.
exclusion_rule: Victory without sovereignty transfer, or a transfer only foretold/feared but not effected in the locator, does not count.

label: Primordial divine rebellion
inclusion_rule: Inside the frozen locator, subordinate/younger divine beings explicitly act in insubordination or rebellion against established divine authority.
exclusion_rule: Retrospective references, external episodes, monster attacks, or sovereign combat lacking an insubordination frame do not count.

label: Divine authority object/power seized
inclusion_rule: A concrete symbol, object, named power, office-token, or explicitly transferable authority of divine rule is stolen, seized, or illicitly appropriated.
exclusion_rule: Generic victory, ordinary weapon theft, or legitimate kingship transfer without seizure does not count.

label: Immortality-giving message/object intercepted
inclusion_rule: An immortality/rejuvenation opportunity is lost because a message, object, substance, or agent is diverted, stolen, substituted, or intercepted.
exclusion_rule: A hero simply fails a quest or violates a prohibition without interception does not count.

label: Snake/reptile renewal contrasts human mortality
inclusion_rule: Snake/reptile skin-renewal, rejuvenation, or immortality is explicitly contrasted with human mortality or lost human renewal.
exclusion_rule: A serpent associated with death or healing without explicit human-mortality contrast does not count.

label: Forbidden act introduces/locks human mortality
inclusion_rule: A prohibited act/transgression is explicitly causal in introducing or fixing human mortality.
exclusion_rule: General punishment or hardship after transgression without mortality causation does not count.

label: First death etiological event
inclusion_rule: Narrative explicitly explains the first human death or how dying first entered human existence.
exclusion_rule: Any famous death that is not etiological does not count.

label: Failed explicit immortality quest
inclusion_rule: A human/hero deliberately seeks immortality or permanent escape from death and fails.
exclusion_rule: General search for healing, youth, or survival without immortality goal does not count.

label: Substance/object confers immortality or rejuvenation
inclusion_rule: A plant, food, drink, object, or material is explicitly capable of conferring immortality or major rejuvenation.
exclusion_rule: Ordinary medicine/food or divine immortality by status alone does not count.

label: Mortality follows choice/substitution/message error
inclusion_rule: A choice, substitution, mistaken/changed message, or decision structure explicitly determines human mortality instead of immortality.
exclusion_rule: Interception by another agent is coded MORT_IMMORTALITY_INTERCEPTED; unrelated bad choice does not count.

label: Humans lose a possible immortal state
inclusion_rule: Derived summary when a specific coded event establishes that humans once possessed or could have possessed immortality and lost it.
exclusion_rule: Never count alongside the specific loss mechanism in primary similarity.

label: Living descent to realm of dead
inclusion_rule: A living human/deity intentionally enters a realm explicitly associated with the dead.
exclusion_rule: Dream/vision only or ordinary cave journey not identified with the dead does not count.

label: Sequential gates/checkpoints
inclusion_rule: Entry/descent requires passage through two or more explicitly ordered gates/checkpoints.
exclusion_rule: A single threshold or unordered obstacles do not count.

label: Loss of clothing/power/status during descent
inclusion_rule: Entrant is progressively or explicitly stripped of clothing, insignia, powers, or status as part of entry/descent.
exclusion_rule: Voluntary disguise or loss unrelated to underworld entry does not count.

label: Return impossible or condition-bound
inclusion_rule: Return from death/underworld is explicitly impossible or depends on a stated condition, substitution, test, or rule.
exclusion_rule: Ordinary difficulty escaping does not count.

label: Formal judgment/evaluation of dead
inclusion_rule: The dead undergo explicit judgment, evaluation, weighing, trial, or formal status allocation.
exclusion_rule: Automatic destination by social category without an evaluative process does not count.

label: River/barrier/ferryman threshold
inclusion_rule: Access to or exit from the realm of the dead requires crossing a named/functional river, barrier, bridge, or ferryman threshold.
exclusion_rule: Any water encountered during travel does not count.

label: Underworld food/drink binds entrant
inclusion_rule: Eating/drinking in the realm of the dead explicitly creates belonging, obligation, or inability/constraint on return.
exclusion_rule: Underworld feasting without return consequence does not count.

label: Return explicitly linked to seasonal/fertility cycle
inclusion_rule: A return/absence cycle involving the underworld is explicitly tied in the narrative or ritual explanation to seasonal or fertility recurrence.
exclusion_rule: Modern allegorical interpretation alone does not count; the link must be source-supported.

label: First/essential fire transferred to humans
inclusion_rule: A narrative explains acquisition/transfer of culturally essential fire to humans.
exclusion_rule: Ordinary fire use or divine fire without human acquisition does not count.

label: Writing/script introduced to humans
inclusion_rule: A deity/hero/ancestor explicitly introduces writing or script to humans.
exclusion_rule: Spoken language, naming, divination marks, or generic knowledge without writing do not count.

label: Language/naming system introduced to humans
inclusion_rule: A narrative explicitly explains introduction/assignment of human language, names, or a symbolic communication system.
exclusion_rule: Writing/script is CULT_WRITING_GIFT; ordinary teaching in an already linguistic society does not count.

label: Agriculture/crops introduced
inclusion_rule: Cultivation, staple crops/seeds, or agricultural practice is explicitly introduced to humans by a named agent/event.
exclusion_rule: Wild plant discovery or ordinary farming instruction without origin frame does not count.

label: Residual craft/technology introduced
inclusion_rule: A craft or technology other than fire, writing/language, or agriculture is explicitly introduced to humans.
exclusion_rule: Use the more specific fire/writing/language/agriculture motif when applicable; do not double-count the same transfer here.

label: Cultural good acquired through deception/theft
inclusion_rule: A culturally important good is acquired for humans through explicit deception, theft, trickery, or rule-breaking by an agent.
exclusion_rule: Do not infer a 'trickster archetype' from character identity; code only the narrated acquisition mechanism.

label: Cultural knowledge/good initially withheld
inclusion_rule: A culturally important knowledge/technology/good is explicitly forbidden, monopolized, hidden, or withheld from humans before acquisition.
exclusion_rule: Scarcity or ignorance without an intentional withholding structure does not count.

label: Benefactor punished for aiding humans
inclusion_rule: An agent is explicitly punished because they transferred/provided a cultural good or knowledge to humans.
exclusion_rule: Punishment for unrelated misconduct does not count.

label: Source agent is nonhuman/supernatural
inclusion_rule: Derived metadata flag classifying the source agent after a specific cultural-transfer motif is coded.
exclusion_rule: Never include as an additional primary similarity motif because it mechanically overlaps many transfer motifs.
